title: Failover controller: emit structured audit events for recommend/execute/rollback
author: Benji Okafor
commits: failover/controller: emit audit events for recommend/execute/rollback
auth: plumb actor identity (user/service) into controller context
observability: add sampling + cardinality guardrails for audit tags
docs: add notes for on-call on where to find audit events
release_notes: - Adds structured audit events for failover recommendations, executions, and rollbacks; events include actor, scope, reason, evidence links, and decision IDs for incident timelines.
description: Summary: This PR adds first-class, structured audit events for the regional failover automation path. The controller now emits events for (1) recommendations (dry-run + live evaluation), (2) executions (policy flips / routing changes), and (3) rollbacks (manual or automated), with consistent IDs so we can correlate a full decision chain across controller logs, dashboards, and incident timelines. Motivation: During rehearsals and early staging drills we had gaps answering basic questions quickly: who/what flipped traffic, what signals were present at the time, what guardrail prevented/allowed the action, and whether the rollback was due to hold-down timers vs recovery signals. Support also has an active enterprise ask for “audit evidence of failover actions” (SUP-25444). This change provides a stable v1 event schema with explicit redaction rules and retention-friendly sinks. Scope/Non-scope: This PR only emits audit events and adds the wiring/compat layer; it does not change trigger hierarchy evaluation or rollback semantics (those are implemented elsewhere; see ENG-2416). It also does not expose audit events to customers directly; internal consumers (incident-bot, timeline tooling, dashboards) will subscribe via the event stream. Design details: Event schema: failover_audit_event.v1. Required fields: event_id (uuid), decision_id (uuid, stable across recommend->execute->rollback when applicable), emitted_at (RFC3339), environment (staging|prod), action (recommend|execute|rollback), outcome (no_op|approved|denied|completed|failed), actor_type (service|user), actor_id (service name or user email hash), actor_display (best-effort, internal only), tenant_scope (hosted_global|tenant:<id>|dedicated_pool:<id>), route_scope (api_route:<name>|gateway_cluster:<name>), from_region, to_region, policy_id, policy_version, reason (enum; see below), evidence (list of short strings; each entry is a stable “signal ref” string, not raw metrics). Optional fields: approval (required|bypassed|granted|rejected), dry_run (true|false), guardrails_triggered (list), rollback_of_event_id, error_code, error_message (truncated), links (dashboard URL, runbook URL, incident timeline URL when present). Reason enum (v1): reachability_failed, error_burn_rate, latency_burn_rate, capacity_exhaustion, control_plane_degraded, operator_initiated, recovery_confirmed, guardrail_rate_limited, guardrail_hold_down, guardrail_tenant_limit, unknown. Evidence format: evidence items are compact references like signal:reachability/probe=perf-canary/us-east->eu-west status=fail window=60s or signal:burn/5xx rate=14x window=5m. We intentionally do not embed high-cardinality labels (tenant_id raw, request_id, hostnames) in the audit event body. Privacy & security: 1) actor_id: for user actors, we store a stable hash of the user principal (sha256 with internal salt); actor_display is included for internal viewing but excluded from the OTLP sink (configurable) and is redacted in log output by default. 2) request payloads: no request bodies, prompts, or customer data are logged. 3) tenant scope: dedicated pools use the internal pool ID; hosted tenants are represented as tenant:<uuid> only when action affects a single tenant and the config explicitly enables it (default off in prod). Sinks: This adds a pluggable sink with two implementations: Kafka (primary for prod, used by incident timeline + incident-bot) and OTLP (optional for staging/dev, to visualize in trace backends). Both are behind feature flags: failover.audit.enabled (default false) and failover.audit.sink (kafka|otlp|log). Failure handling: audit emission is best-effort and must not block failover execution. The sink uses a bounded queue + drop counters. If the queue is full, we drop with an internal metric increment and emit a single warning per 60s (to avoid log spam during events). Metrics: failover_audit_emitted_total{action,outcome,reason} and failover_audit_dropped_total{reason}. (Note: labels are bounded; no tenant label.) Testing: - Unit tests for schema validation and redaction behavior. - Controller integration test asserts decision_id stability across recommend->execute flow, and that rollback events include rollback_of_event_id. - Config schema validation ensures audit is disabled by default. Rollout plan: 1) Enable audit emission in staging with sink=log for game-day rehearsals. 2) Enable in prod for a limited set of routes (hosted chat+embeddings) with sink=kafka and sampling=1.0 (bounded by queue). 3) Incident-bot PR will subscribe to the Kafka topic to post summaries into #incidents and #eng-sre (tracked separately). Notes for reviewers: This PR intentionally keeps the v1 schema conservative. If you think we need additional evidence fields (e.g., “top contributing signal”), please request now—adding fields later is easy, but renaming/removing fields will be painful. Example event (execute): action=execute outcome=completed actor_type=service actor_id=failover-controller decision_id=7a6e... tenant_scope=hosted_global from_region=us-east to_region=eu-west reason=reachability_failed evidence=[signal:reachability/probe=perf-canary/us-east->eu-west status=fail window=60s, signal:burn/5xx rate=12x window=5m] guardrails_triggered=[guardrail_hold_down:passed, guardrail_rate_limited:passed]. Review conversation highlights: - Miles requested decision_id be stable even when we “recommend only” (dry-run). Implemented by generating decision_id at the beginning of evaluation and threading through actions. - Allison requested we avoid adding tenant_tier labels to emitted metrics due to cardinality risk. Adjusted metrics to only include action/outcome/reason and added a separate structured field tenant_scope in the audit event payload (not as a metric label). - Devon asked for event links to be “late-bound” (incident URL may not exist at time of emission). Implemented links as optional; timeline tooling can enrich later using event_id/decision_id. - Rafael requested explicit guardrail recording (rate limit/hold-down) even when action is denied. Added guardrails_triggered to recommend events as well (outcome=denied). Follow-ups: - Add incident-timeline enrichment and annotations using these audit events (see PR-19844). - Reduce audit reason values and align with dashboard terminology once ADR-042 language is finalized.
notes: Default config keeps audit disabled in prod until we finish consumer rollout (incident-bot + timeline tooling).
Event schema version is v1; future changes should add v2 alongside v1 rather than mutate fields.
